content: HOT-17, also known as 2,5-dimethoxy-4-(β-isobutylthio)-N-hydroxyphenethylamine, is a psychedelic compound belonging to the phenethylamine class, specifically within the 2C family. It is believed to have been first synthesized by Alexander Shulgin and was documented in his book PIHKAL (Phenethylamines I Have Known and Loved). The full chemical name of HOT-17 is 2-[4-(2-isobutylthio)-2,5-dimethoxyphenyl]-N-hydroxyethanamine. Its molecular structure is closely related to 2C-T-17 and other compounds in the HOT series, with the most structurally similar analogs being HOT-2 and HOT-7. The typical dosage range for HOT-17 is between 70 and 120 milligrams, and its effects generally last for approximately 12 to 18 hours, as described by Shulgin. The substance is known to induce time distortion and general psychedelic effects. Additionally, it is reported to have minimal to no physical discomfort or body load associated with its use.
